text:
Priya (support): FYI - Customer "AcmeHealth" on Dedicated pool dp-us-west-2-7 is reporting big p95/p99 regressions after a traffic burst ~2026-02-15T13:04Z. They say a lot of requests were queued and some timed out. Attaching the repro notes and a short logs snippet.

Priya (support): Repro steps the customer provided: 1) spike ~2000 RPS sustained for ~2m; 2) many calls hit /v1/generate with model 'redwood-open-13b-q4' with seq len ~1024; 3) observed 502 / attach timeouts and 504s for streaming.

Priya (support): Logs (scrubbed):
```
2026-02-15T13:04:22Z ERROR attach_timeout request_id=abc123 pool=dp-us-west-2-7 attach_time_ms=3500 queued_for_ms=2100
2026-02-15T13:04:23Z WARN provision_throttle pool=dp-us-west-2-7 throttle_reason=attach_rate_limit current_attempts=12
2026-02-15T13:04:25Z INFO request_queued request_id=def456 queue_pos=18 estimated_warmup_ms=4200
```

Evan (oncall): Ack — looking now. Do we have the pool's autoscaler events/metrics (attach latency, provision queue length, warm_pool size) for that window? Any 5xx spike counts?

Priya (support): 5xx spike to ~1.8% from baseline 0.1% during the burst. Link to dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dash/pools/dp-us-west-2-7 (sent).

Liang (eng-sre): I pulled the autoscaler logs for dp-us-west-2-7. Early suspicion: warm pool was at 0 when the burst hit, and scale-up actions were rate-limited by the provision throttle. Looks like we hit the per-pool attach rate limit which then backed off provisioning, so requests queued behind a cold attach path.

Liang (eng-sre): Pool status snapshot around spike:
```
$ redwoodctl pool status dp-us-west-2-7 --short
pool: dp-us-west-2-7
state: ACTIVE
min_capacity: 2
current_warm: 0
current_attaching: 8
queued_requests: 240
p95_attach_ms: 2100
p99_attach_ms: 6700
provision_throttle: true
```

Marco (platform): Confirmed in infra metrics: provisioning queue length jumped and the provisioner returned "throttle" due to burst policy: max_attach_rate_per_pool=10/min. There was also a concurrent region-wide coldstart window from a previous maintenance.

OpsBot: :rotating_light: alert: provision_throttle fired for dp-us-west-2-7 at 2026-02-15T13:04:22Z (rule: pool_provision_throttle_v2).

Evan (oncall): OK — root cause looks like combined factors: (1) warm_pool left at 0 (config drift or recent deploy), (2) aggressive per-pool attach rate limits that prevented rapid warmup, (3) concurrent region maintenance reduced spare capacity. Result: many requests hit cold attach path and p99 attach skyrocketed -> p95/p99 request latency regression.

Evan (oncall): Immediate mitigation options (short-lived):
- Increase pool.min_capacity to reduce chance of 0 warm replicas.
- Temporarily bump max_attach_rate_per_pool for this pool to allow faster warmup (risk: provisioning thundering herd).
- Enable customer fallback: route AcmeHealth to hosted-tier model variant until pool stabilizes.
- Short term: bump dedicated pool burst_capacity/receive emergency credits to pre-warm GPUs.

Liang (eng-sre): I can push a quick autoscaler patch: raise min_capacity from 2 -> 6 and set warm_replenish=true for 15m. Example patch (will be applied to dp-us-west-2-7 only):
```
# autoscaler patch
pool: dp-us-west-2-7
min_capacity: 6
warm_replenish: true
max_attach_rate_per_pool: 30  # temporary
```

Liang (eng-sre): Command: `redwoodctl pool patch dp-us-west-2-7 --from-file quickfix.yml`

Marco (platform): I prefer to slowly ramp max_attach_rate_per_pool to avoid creating a provisioning spike. I'll apply min_capacity bump first and watch. If we still see queue > 50 after 3m, then I'll nudge attach rate.

Marco (platform): Applying min_capacity bump now (canary to pool node group A only).

Marco (platform): `ok` — canary applied to node-group A. Observability: warm_count increased from 0 -> 3 in ~90s. queued_requests dropping from 240 -> 60. p95_attach_ms trending down.

Priya (support): Customer on the thread says latency is improving, less 5xx. They're grateful but asking about why min_capacity dropped to 0 in the first place.

Marta (customer-success): I spoke to customer briefly — they want to understand SLA and cost impact. If we keep min_capacity at 6 for longer, we should bill the committed nodes vs justify as mitigation. Customer is okay with temporary change.

Evan (oncall): Action items:
- Liang to open a bug for autoscaler config drift/backfill that allowed warm pool to be zero (owner: Liang).
- Marco to run a retrospective check on per-pool attach rate throttles and consider adaptive burst windows (owner: Marco).
- Priya/Marta to confirm with AcmeHealth about fallback to hosted model if we need more time (owner: Priya).
- Evan to document incident and update runbook with new quick-mitigation steps (owner: Evan).

Liang (eng-sre): Created bug: RW-PLAT-6521 "autoscaler allowed warm_pool=0 after deploy -> scale-up starvation" — linking autoscaler diff and current logs.

Marco (platform): Postmortem note: consider introducing a "prewarm safety floor" setting that is automatically enforced for enterprise customers with SLAs so min_capacity can't be set to 0 without an approval.

Evan (oncall): Nice work triaging quickly. For follow-up: schedule a 30m sync tomorrow with autoscaler, platform, and support to pick longer-term mitigations (adaptive attach rate, burst_capacity policies, and warm_pool health checks). I'll create the calendar invite and tag stakeholders.

Priya (support): Thanks all — closing loop with customer now. Will update thread when customer confirms final state. :thumbsup:

Marco (platform): We should also add a dashboard panel to show "p95_attach_ms vs warm_count" so this pattern surfaces earlier.

Evan (oncall): Marking this thread as incident:severity=sev3 and adding to eng-oncall board.

Priya (support): Customer confirmed after 12m latency returned to baseline. No further errors. Thanks team.
